name: Mexico (federal ISR + IMSS employee quotas)
kernel_parts_used: Schedule (band versions of both tarifas: progressive, mono, convex, lipschitz)
Table (1.1: cuotas fijas as a lookup table, contiguous/valuesMono/agreesWith/disagreements)
kernel_gaps: CuotaFijaTable: tarifas printed as (límite inferior, cuota fija, % sobre excedente) with independently rounded cuotas; the kernel 1.1 Table now checks the cuotas (cuotas152_*), the evaluation itself stays local (MxTax.Basic.tarifaTicks), proved within -3.87/+0.34 centavos of the kernel Schedule
Amounts in centavos with limits at x.01 (kernel assumes whole units; worked with centavos as the unit)
Contribution rates finer than a basis point (0.375 %, 0.625 %, 1.125 %): IMSS written locally (MxTax.Wage.imssOf)
Day-based contribution with a unit of account changing mid-year (UMA 2024 in January, 2025 from February)
Monthly all-or-nothing credit with an income cut-off and a monthly/annual reconciliation (subsidio para el empleo); kernel Credit has tapers, not cliffs
Single-rate-on-the-whole-amount tables (RESICO art. 113-F) and regime exit by month count
Optional dividend gross-up with a non-refundable credit (art. 140) chosen per taxpayer

validation.referee: OECD TW 2025 (Taxing Wages 2026, year 2025); same 56/41/48 from ~/cmp20/harness/oecd_check20.py
validation.notes: Income-tax lines CGTC/CGITLETC/CGITFP 24/24 exact (to the centavo before rounding); SLT, CTGG 16/16; EECSSC 1/8 exact and 8/8 within 1 % by default (calendar UMA, +1..+3 MXN, F2), 8/8 exact with mxImss=oecd; THP 0/8 within 1 % because the OECD leaves cesantía y vejez (1.125 %) out of SSC (F1).
not run: the SAT simuladores need a login (e.firma/contraseña); none queried

headline: Mexico's income tax matches the OECD to the centavo, but its employment subsidy (received by about 6.1 million workers) stops dead at 10,171 pesos a month, 1.2 minimum wages: ten pesos more annual pay can cost 5,213, with a dead zone of about 5 % of pay above the cut-off.
